newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PLDT may cut international call tariffs.
newsitem.headline: PLDT may cut international call tariffs.

text.p: Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co (PLDT), the country's largest phone company, facing increasing competition from newer rivals may cut international call tariffs by up to 20 percent next year, an official said.
The new rates will come into effect after the company implements a metering system for its domestic calls, PLDT executive vice-president Jose de Jesus told reporters on Friday.
PLDT, a virtual monopoly until the government recently liberalised the telecommunications industry, uses several old exchanges that do not record the duration of a call.
It therefore charges a flat monthly rate for domestic calls and makes up for the difference in revenues by charging higher tariffs on international calls.
The arrival of competition forced PLDT to launch on a massive modernisation and expansion programme which has put in place modern exchanges that can meter calls.
De Jesus said the metering system would not mean higher telephone bills for a large number of its domestic call clients.

"The impact of the metering scheme is that 60 percent of present subscribers will not be paying more than what they are paying now, assuming that they maintain present calling patterns. The rest will pay more because they use the phones more," he said.
The metering of local calls will have to be approved by the National Telecommunications Commission before PLDT can implement it.
